subject: Temporary access exception for deleted session data - Acme Analytics
messages:
From: Toby Ellis <toby.ellis@acme-analytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-security@acme-analytics.com
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: need access to deleted session slices for investigation

Hi Dylan / Maya,

We ran into a production issue this morning where a small subset of user sessions show garbled outputs and we believe a sequence of tokens for a few sessions was removed by the workspace retention job. We have a short reproduction that points to three session ids (see attached session_index.csv). For our SREs to reproduce the bug end-to-end they need the raw session slices and model KV cache that were removed.

Can Redwood restore those slices or grant a temporary retention override so we can pull the data for debugging? We understand this is sensitive; we can sign an NDA amendment or follow any required process. Our timeline is tight — would appreciate an ETA for next steps.

Attachment: acme_debug_request.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: session_index.csv (csv)

—
Toby Ellis
Head of Platform Reliability, Acme Analytics
T: +1 415 555 0198

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: need access to deleted session slices for investigation

Looping internal team for quick triage — customer (Acme) is asking for a temporary exception to workspace retention to recover three deleted session slices. Key asks below:

- Can infra restore the slices or create a read-only temporary retention override?
- If we can, what controls/logging will be in place (who accesses, how long, audit trail)?
- Legal: what approvals/documents do we need before we hand over data (NDA addendum, POA, etc.)?

We should assume data contains PII until proven otherwise. Customer is able to sign paperwork quickly if needed. Can we get a quick go/no-go within the day? If yes, I'll coordinate with Acme to schedule the extraction window.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: need access to deleted session slices for investigation

Short answer: technically possible with safeguards, but requires coordination and will be manual. Details: 

- We have immutable S3 backups for deleted slices for 30 days before deep purge. If the sessions fell within that window we can restore the objects to a temp bucket.
- I can implement a temporary retention-override flag at the object-level so that the object is excluded from the lifecycle job for X hours. This is not yet a self-serve flow — I would need to run a patch (temp_retention_change.patch) and trigger an extraction job.
- Auditability: every action can be logged to the admin audit log (we'll capture operator identity, source IP, and bucket object versions). We should also restrict access to a read-only role scoped to the extraction job.
- Est. work: ~3 hours to validate objects + 1 hour to run extraction and handover.

Constraints / questions: 
- If the data includes developer-provided embeddings or function-call payloads, that may include customer PII — legal needs to sign off on permitted sharing.
- We need an approved retention-override ticket in the tracker (JIRA-INC-5892) and an authorized approver.

On Wed, Apr 8, 2026 at 10:05 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Looping internal team for quick triage — customer (Acme) is asking for a temporary exception...

—
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Apr 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: need access to deleted session slices for investigation

Thanks for the quick heads-up. From a legal/compliance perspective, we can approve a narrowly scoped, time-limited retention override provided the following are completed before any data is accessed: 

1) Approved JIRA ticket assigned to "Retention Overrides" sprint (JIRA-INC-5892) documenting reason and session ids.
2) Customer-signed Addendum to the Data Processing Agreement (DPA) specifying the purpose, scope, retention window, and acknowledgement that Redwood will treat the data as potentially sensitive. We can accept an e-signature.
3) An RBAC change that creates a temporary read-only role limited to the extraction job and two named engineers.
4) Audit plan: operator, timestamps, and hashes of objects to be recorded and attached to the ticket.

If the customer cannot sign the DPA addendum immediately, we can do a controlled remote debug: customer exports the minimal reproduction and we debug in their environment. That is slower but avoids data transfer.

Once we have these items, Legal will approve within 2 business hours. If you want me to draft the addendum I can send a template today.

—
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Toby Ellis <toby.ellis@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: acme-security@acme-analytics.com, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 15:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: need access to deleted session slices for investigation — next steps

Hi Toby — thanks for the details and the attachments. Quick summary and proposed plan so we can move forward safely: 

What we can do now:
- We can restore the three deleted session objects from immutable backups and exclude them from lifecycle for a 12-hour window. Vivek estimates ~4 hours total to validate and extract.
- Access will be strictly limited to two Redwood engineers (named below) with a temporary read-only role; all actions will be logged.

What we need from Acme (to proceed):
1) Sign a short DPA addendum (I attached the template).
2) Confirm that the two session ids in session_index.csv are the only ones needed.
3) Provide a point-of-contact and their phone number for the extraction window.

If you prefer not to sign the addendum, we can attempt remote-debugging guidance instead (slower). Let me know which path you prefer.

Attachments: acme_debug_request.pdf, session_index.csv, DPA_addendum_template.docx (will send in separate email)

Named engineers for access (will be provisioned in RBAC): Vivek Kulkarni, Arun S. (Redwood infra oncall)

Next steps: If Acme confirms and signs, Laura will sign off within 2 business hours and Vivek will execute the extraction. I'll create the JIRA ticket (JIRA-INC-5892) and post the audit artifacts to the ticket.

Thanks — aiming to minimize blast radius and keep everything auditable.

—
Dylan Brooks
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0133
[Attachment: temp_retention_change.patch (patch)]
